gap: No result ChatGPT got states that ProjectorCentral measured the XGIMI MoGo 4 at only about 400 ISO lumens in Performance mode, where its fan read 48.2–52.4 dBA, and that its quiet Standard mode (31.1–32.2 dBA in a 30.5 dBA room) puts out just 258–270 lumens. The same lab measured the Nebula Mars 3 Air at 372–399 ANSI lumens with the fan at about 40 dBA in every mode.
standout_why: I opened TechRadar (28 Oct 2026; the page was cut off and had no figures), RTINGS' best-portable list (only a navigation shell loaded, with no numbers), a2zcheck (maker claims only, says nothing about fan noise or power modes), and itechguides' MoGo 4 vs Capsule 3 page (it says outright that it has no same-condition lab test and gives no dB figures). I could not load Wirecutter, the only cited page, at nytimes.com or through the proxy. ChatGPT's answer itself repeats only rated lumens (450 ISO, 400 ANSI, 200 ANSI, 550 ISO) and never mentions measured output, fan noise or what each power mode trades away.
decides: ChatGPT's choice of the MoGo 4 as best all-round is shaky on these numbers. It reaches about its rated brightness only in Performance mode, where ProjectorCentral measured the fan at about 50 dBA and the reviewer called that mode too green to use. In its quiet mode it gives about 260 lumens, close to the Capsule 3's 201 lumens in Bright mode. In ProjectorCentral's test the Mars 3 Air kept about 380–399 lumens at about 40 dBA and ran 3 h 10 min on battery, which backs it as the movie pick. The Capsule 3 lost about 40% of its brightness on battery (ProjectorReviews; The Hook Up measured 161 to 112 lumens), so it suits a fully dark room only.

findings.label: Measured brightness by power mode (ISO 21118)
findings.value: Performance 400–404 lm; Standard 258–270 lm; ECO 151–154 lm (rated 450 ISO)
findings.source_title: XGIMI MoGo 4 1080P DLP Projector review, ProjectorCentral (Nikki Kahl, 2025-08-25)
findings.note: Measured in Standard, Movie, Game and User picture modes in each power mode. The reviewer says Performance mode boosts brightness 'at the expense of color' and that all modes look quite green. The review does not say whether Performance mode is available on battery.

findings.label: Fan noise by power mode
findings.value: Performance 48.2–52.4 dBA; Standard 31.1–32.2 dBA; ECO 31.0–31.6 dBA (XGIMI rates 28 dBA)
findings.source_title: XGIMI MoGo 4 1080P DLP Projector review, ProjectorCentral (Nikki Kahl, 2025-08-25)
findings.note: Measured about 3 ft from the front, rear, left and right. Room noise floor 30.5 dBA, so Standard and ECO are barely above the room.

findings.label: Input lag (1080p60, Game picture mode)
findings.value: 22.1 ms with Game Mode on; 44.8 ms with PC Mode only; 38.8 ms with both (rated 20 ms)
findings.source_title: XGIMI MoGo 4 1080P DLP Projector review, ProjectorCentral (Nikki Kahl, 2025-08-25)

findings.label: Battery runtime
findings.value: About 2.5 h in ECO; Standard mode lasted through a 90-minute film
findings.source_title: XGIMI MoGo 4 1080P DLP Projector review, ProjectorCentral (Nikki Kahl, 2025-08-25)
findings.note: Reviewer's own use. ECO mode gives about 151 lm per the brightness table. The review gives no exact runtime for Standard mode.

findings.label: Measured brightness (ANSI, AC power)
findings.value: Conference 399 lm; Standard 383 lm; Game 382 lm; Movie 372 lm (rated 400 ANSI); 145 lm on battery in Eco, Standard picture mode
findings.source_title: Anker Nebula Mars 3 Air 1080P DLP Projector review, ProjectorCentral (Brian Nadel, 2024-03-14)

findings.label: Fan noise, input lag, battery runtime
findings.value: 40.3 dBA in Conference mode, 40.1 dBA in Movie, 40.0 dBA in Eco; input lag 44.1 ms; 3 h 10 min on a full charge in Eco (rated 2.5 h)
findings.source_title: Anker Nebula Mars 3 Air 1080P DLP Projector review, ProjectorCentral (Brian Nadel, 2024-03-14)
findings.note: Anker rates 28 dB under ISO 7779; the reviewer did not verify that. Runtime was measured in Eco at 145 lm.

findings.label: Second lab: brightness, contrast, fan, runtime
findings.value: 450 ANSI lm plugged in; 203 lm on battery (Eco); 373:1 contrast; 42.4 dB fan; 3 h 23 min at 128 lm
findings.source_title: Ultimate Portable Projector Comparison – 2024 Update, The Hook Up (2024-09-12)
findings.note: The Hook Up's own measurements. The page gives no fan-measurement distance for this model.

findings.label: Measured brightness by picture mode (ANSI, AC power)
findings.value: Bright 201 lm; Custom 145; Movie 142; Standard 131; Game 125 (rated 200 ANSI); about 40% lower on battery
findings.source_title: Nebula Capsule 3 series portable LED projector review, ProjectorReviews (Philip Boyle, 2024-03-29)
findings.note: LED 1080p Google TV model. The roughly 40% battery drop is the reviewer's stated figure. No fan-noise or runtime measurement is given.

findings.label: Second lab: brightness, contrast, fan, runtime
findings.value: 161 ANSI lm plugged in; 112 lm on battery (Eco); 357:1 contrast; fan 38.3 dB at 18 in, full brightness; 2 h 53 min on battery at 112 lm; 7 h 14 min with a 20,000 mAh power bank
findings.source_title: Ultimate Portable Projector Comparison – 2024 Update, The Hook Up (2024-09-12)
findings.note: The page calls it the LED Capsule 3 but does not name the OS. 161 lm is about 80% of the 200 lm claim.

findings.label: Measured brightness, noise, input lag, contrast
findings.value: 370–390 ANSI lm in standard configurations (rated 550 ISO); Eco under 200 lm; under 40 dB close to the projector in standard mode; input lag 40 ms; contrast 975:1 before calibration, 735:1 after
findings.source_title: XGIMI MoGo 4 Laser test review, Laurent Willen (published 2025-06-07, updated 2026-01-13)
findings.note: Laurent Willen's own measurements. He calls Performance mode 'very noisy' but gives no dB figure for it. Battery: about 1 h 30 to 2 h at standard brightness, from his use. Game mode was not working yet when he tested.
